### CLAUDE (2026-06-12T15:25:33.628Z)

Done. The POSTOFFICE_UK dataset is built, validated against the live Optimization v2 API, and documented.

## What I built

A self-contained generator (`POSTOFFICE_UK/scripts/generate-synthetic-data.mjs`) modeled on the COCA_COLA-FEMSA approach — circular service area, coordinates snapped to real roads via NB.ai reverse geocoding — adapted to a **depot-based** use case. It produced five files in `POSTOFFICE_UK/data/`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `input.json` | Optimization v2 body — `locations` (idx 0 = depot), `depots`, `vehicles`, `jobs`, `options.routing.mode: "car"` |
| `jobs.csv` | 300 delivery stops, route-planner-import ready |
| `depots.csv` | The single depot |
| `vehicles.csv` | 30-van fleet with shift/working-time/break columns |
| `boundary.geojson` | The 50-mile service-area circle + depot point |

## Key decisions

- **Depot:** `E6 7FF` → geocoded to *Hornet Way, Beckton, London* (51.5155, 0.0825) on the eastern edge of Greater London.
- **Service area:** 50-mile (80.5 km) radius circle, centre-biased sampling (denser in inner London — realistic for postal delivery, fewer wasted samples over the estuary/sea).
- **Fleet:** 30 Mercedes Sprinter vans, **car** profile, shift **06:00–19:00** BST.
- **UK/EU drivers' hours** on every vehicle: `max_working_time: 42300` (11h45m cap) and one mandatory **45-min break** (`service: 2700`) schedulable 10:00–15:00 — i.e. after ~the first 4 hours. NB's break model schedules within a time window rather than off a rolling drive-time counter, so that window is the faithful encoding of "45-min break after 4 hours."
- **Scale:** I used 300 stops / 30 vans as announced defaults (both CLI-overridable via `--jobs` / `--vans`), since you didn't specify counts.

## Validation (live submit, seed 20260626)
Solved cleanly: **12/30** vans used, **296/300** stops assigned, one 45-min break per route, longest route **9.28h** (within the 11.75h cap). The 4 unassigned are far-edge Essex/Kent stops that can't round-trip within the legal limit — the constraint working as intended. (To assign all 300, shrink `--radius-miles` or raise stop density nearer the depot.)

Two notes: I added `boundary.geojson` beyond your four requested files (handy for map visualization — say if you'd rather drop it), and counts/depot are easy to re-run differently. Want me to tune the job/van counts, or tighten the radius so nothing goes unassigned?

Points are rejection-\n// sampled from the polygon's bbox and tested with ray casting so generated\n// coordinates fall inside the actual operating area, not the bounding box.\nconst POLYGON_LNG_LAT = [\n  [-0.1835702, 51.9450549],\n  [-0.3310725, 51.9767945],\n  [-0.548814, 51.9161812],\n  [-0.892986, 51.8366827],\n  [-0.8625491, 51.4895914],\n  [-0.7969925, 51.4443763],\n  [-0.8719143, 51.3260219],\n  [-0.8321121, 51.2454833],\n  [-0.670562, 51.242552],\n  [-0.640125, 51.1765475],\n  [-0.5581793, 51.1970924],\n  [-0.5183771, 51.1075084],\n  [-0.3380965, 51.1177974],\n  [-0.1601572, 51.0913354],\n  [-0.1016245, 51.1045683],\n  [0.1161169, 50.9897576],\n  [0.2519127, 50.8938645],\n  [0.4345346, 50.8982947],\n  [0.5937434, 50.8938645],\n  [0.7599761, 50.948474],\n  [0.8676762, 51.0236416],\n  [1.1205373, 51.0957468],\n  [1.1931178, 51.2923594],\n  [0.7787066, 51.3494248],\n  [0.7108087, 51.3655074],\n  [0.598426, 51.3713542],\n  [0.5117977, 51.3888901],\n  [0.4860433, 51.4108006],\n  [0.5281868, 51.4691772],\n  [0.3877085, 51.4283214],\n  [0.2472301, 51.4487539],\n  [0.1910387, 51.4764691],\n  [0.1207995, 51.50271],\n  [0.191358, 51.5114934],\n  [0.2948437, 51.540759],\n  [0.4853516, 51.5436846],\n  [0.5488542, 51.5816994],\n  [0.5323905, 51.6313631],\n  [0.3583463, 51.6445002],\n  [0.1419671, 51.6445002],\n  [0.2289892, 51.7873033],\n  [0.3066035, 51.896287],\n  [-0.1835702, 51.9450549],\n];\n\nconst BBOX = (() => {\n  let south = Infinity, north = -Infinity, west = Infinity, east = -Infinity;\n  for (const [lng, lat] of POLYGON_LNG_LAT) {\n    if (lat < south) south = lat;\n    if (lat > north) north = lat;\n    if (lng < west)  west  = lng;\n    if (lng > east)  east  = lng;\n  }\n  return { south, north, west, east };\n})();\n\n// Ray-casting point-in-polygon (lng/lat). Polygon edges are treated as outside;\n// coincident points are vanishingly rare for floating-point samples.\nfunction pointInPolygon(lng, lat, ring) {\n  let inside = false;\n  for (let i = 0, j = ring.length - 1; i < ring.length; j = i++) {\n    const [xi, yi] = ring[i];\n    const [xj, yj] = ring[j];\n    const intersects = ((yi > lat) !== (yj > lat)) &&\n      (lng < ((xj - xi) * (lat - yi)) / (yj - yi || 1e-12) + xi);\n    if (intersects) inside = !inside;\n  }\n  return inside;\n}\n\n// Rejection-sample a random point inside the service-area polygon.\nfunction randCoordInPolygon() {\n  for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {\n    const lat = BBOX.south + rng() * (BBOX.north - BBOX.south);\n    const lng = BBOX.west + rng() * (BBOX.east - BBOX.west);\n    if (pointInPolygon(lng, lat, POLYGON_LNG_LAT)) return { lat, lng };\n  }\n  throw new Error('Could not sample a point inside POLYGON_LNG_LAT after 1000 attempts');\n}"

## What changed

- **Sampling area:** swapped the 50-mile circle for your supplied **Greater London + Home Counties** polygon. The script now embeds it as `POLYGON_LNG_LAT`, computes its bbox, and rejection-samples with a ray-casting point-in-polygon test (the same technique as the COCA_COLA-FEMSA generator). The post-snap guard also re-checks containment, so a point the API nudges across the edge is rejected.
- **Removed** the now-irrelevant `--radius-miles` flag and circle/haversine helpers.
- **`boundary.geojson`** now emits your actual polygon (42 vertices) plus the depot point.
- Updated the header docs and README to match.

## Re-validation (seed 20260626, regenerated)

- **All 300 job points verified inside the polygon** (0 outside).
- Submitted to Optimization v2 → solved cleanly: **13 of 30** vans used, **300/300 stops assigned (0 unassigned)**, one 45-min break per route (13 total), longest route **9.18h** (within the 11.75h cap), 1,036 parcels, ~3,808 km.

Tightening the boundary to your polygon (which trims the far Essex/Kent fringes the circle reached) is what let all 300 stops fit within drivers'-hours limits — previously 4 were unassigned.

All five files in `POSTOFFICE_UK/data/` (`input.json`, `jobs.csv`, `depots.csv`, `vehicles.csv`, `boundary.geojson`) are regenerated and consistent. Depot stays at E6 7FF, which sits inside the boundary.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-23T19:51:32.216Z)

The workaround is a single line that strips a doubled percent sign from the style text before parsing it.

## The snippet

```ts
// Fix broken HSL values in the NB style (e.g. "24%%" -> "24%")
const rawText = await response.text();
const fixedText = rawText.replace(/%%/g, '%');
const styleJson = JSON.parse(fixedText);
```

The key line is **`.replace(/%%/g, '%')`**, applied to the raw response text *before* `JSON.parse`.

## What it resolves

The NextBillion map-style endpoint (TomTom-backed) returns color values with a typo — a doubled percent sign in HSL literals, e.g. `"hsl(160, 43%, 24%%)"`. That trailing `%%` is a malformed color value, so when MapLibre/Mapbox GL parses and applies the style it throws an invalid-color / syntax error on load. The regex globally rewrites every `%%` → `%` (`24%%` → `24%`), producing a valid style object that loads cleanly.

The fetch-as-text → sanitize → `JSON.parse` ordering is essential: you can't fix it after parsing because the parse itself (or GL's color parsing) is what fails on the bad literal.

## Where it lives

It appears in **three** projects, with slightly different placement:

| Project | File | Placement |
|---|---|---|
| **schedule_finder** | `src/app/api/map-style/route.ts:51` | Server-side proxy route (canonical) |
| **indoor_mapping** | `app/api/[[...path]]/route.js:223` | Server-side catch-all, `/map-style` branch |
| **loadboard_demo** | `components/Map.tsx:22` | Client-side `fetchFixedStyle` helper |

Notably, **isochrone-map-tool**'s `map-style/route.ts:45` calls `JSON.parse(text)` on **un-sanitized** text — so it's missing this fix and would break the same way if the upstream style still contains `%%`. Want me to add the `.replace(/%%/g, '%')` guard there (and to free-route-planner) for consistency?

### CLAUDE (2026-06-23T19:55:53.069Z)

Here's the expanded snippet showing how the style is loaded leading up to the `response.text()` line, from `schedule_finder/src/app/api/map-style/route.ts:45`:

```ts
try {
  const styleUrl = `${NB_ORIGIN}/tt/style/1/style/22.2.1-9?map=2/basic_street-dark&key=${apiKey}`;
  const response = await fetch(styleUrl, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000) });
  if (!response.ok) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: `Style fetch failed: ${response.status}` }, { status: 502 });
  }
  // Fix broken HSL values in the NB style (e.g. "24%%" -> "24%")
  const rawText = await response.text();
  const fixedText = rawText.replace(/%%/g, '%');
  const styleJson = JSON.parse(fixedText);
```

## The load sequence before the fix

1. **Build the style URL** (line 46) — `NB_ORIGIN` is `https://api.nextbillion.io`, and the path `/tt/style/1/style/22.2.1-9?map=2/basic_street-dark` requests the TomTom-backed dark basic-street style. The API key (`getApiKey()`, line 40) is appended as a query param.

2. **Fetch the style** (line 47) — a server-side `fetch` with a 10-second `AbortSignal.timeout`. This runs in the Next.js API route (not the browser), which is what lets the route strip the API key before the style ever reaches the client.

3. **Guard the response** (lines 48–50) — if the upstream fetch isn't `ok`, it bails out with a 502 rather than trying to parse a non-style body.

4. **Read as text, then sanitize** (lines 52–54) — only after those checks does it pull the body as raw text and apply `.replace(/%%/g, '%')` before `JSON.parse`. Reading as text (not `response.json()`) is what makes the fix possible — you need the raw string to repair the malformed `24%%` HSL literals before parsing.

After this, the parsed `styleJson` goes through `rewriteUrls` (line 62) to swap NB URLs for the local `/api/map-proxy` path, again to keep the API key off the client.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-25T21:11:17.067Z)

Everything's wired through GCP Secret Manager, not a `.env` file. Here's how to check and fix it.

**Your setup** (from terraform):
- Project: `[GCP_PROJECT]`, region: `us-central1`
- Cloud Run service: `glwas-demo`
- Secret: `glwas-demo-nb-api-key` (the Cloud Run env var `NB_API_KEY` points at version `latest`)

## 1. Check the secret exists and has a value

```bash
# Does the secret exist, and does it have a non-empty latest version?
gcloud secrets versions access latest \
  --secret=glwas-demo-nb-api-key \
  --project=[GCP_PROJECT]
```
If this prints your key → the secret is fine, problem is the service wiring (go to step 3). If it errors "NOT_FOUND" or prints empty → the secret/value is missing (step 2).

## 2. Check the running revision actually has the env var wired

This is the most common cause: if the live revision was deployed by `gcloud run deploy <image>` (instead of `terraform apply`), it can drop the secret env binding.

```bash
gcloud run services describe glwas-demo \
  --region=us-central1 --project=[GCP_PROJECT] \
  --format='yaml(spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)'
```
You want to see an `NB_API_KEY` entry with a `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` → `glwas-demo-nb-api-key`. If `NB_API_KEY` is missing here, the container never gets the value regardless of the secret.

## 3. Fix

**Preferred — re-apply terraform** (it owns both the secret and the env wiring):
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/GLWAS/terraform
terraform apply
```
Make sure `nb_api_key` in `terraform.tfvars` is set to a real key.

**Quick manual fix without terraform** — set the secret value, then bind it to the service:
```bash
# (a) put a value in the secret (creates the secret if needed)
printf 'YOUR_REAL_NB_KEY' | gcloud secrets versions add glwas-demo-nb-api-key \
  --data-file=- --project=[GCP_PROJECT]

# (b) point the service env var at it (forces a new revision)
gcloud run services update glwas-demo \
  --region=us-central1 --project=[GCP_PROJECT] \
  --update-secrets=NB_API_KEY=glwas-demo-nb-api-key:latest
```

After either fix, Cloud Run rolls a new revision — reload the app and re-run the comparison.

One thing to confirm: **does the deploy SA have access to the secret?** Terraform grants `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` to `glwas-demo-sa` (`main.tf:70`). If you changed the service account, the container can't read the secret even when it exists — re-running `terraform apply` restores that grant.

Want me to run the two read-only check commands (steps 1–2) for you now to pinpoint which case it is?

Done. The script is now fully localized to Chicago and parses cleanly, with no remaining Warsaw/Polish/CEST references.

## Timezone changes (`generate-synthetic-data-wise.mjs`)

| Item | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Header comment | "FEMSA Polska … greater Warsaw region" | "Coca-Cola … greater Chicago region" |
| Polygon comment | "Greater Warsaw service-area polygon" | "Greater Chicago service-area polygon" |
| Offset constant | `WARSAW_TZ_OFFSET_HOURS = -6` (mislabeled CEST) | `CHICAGO_TZ_OFFSET_HOURS = -5` (CDT) |
| Format fn | `fmtPLDateTime` → `timeZone: 'Europe/Warsaw'` | `fmtCTDateTime` → `timeZone: 'America/Chicago'` |
| Break/comment labels | CEST | CDT |
| Console log | "Europe/Warsaw, CEST UTC+-6" | "America/Chicago, CDT UTC-5" |

## One correctness note worth flagging
I changed the offset from **−6 to −5**. The planning date (June 29) is in **Central Daylight Time = UTC−5**, but the old constant was −6 (standard time). Now the timestamp math (`ymdToUnixUTC`, which does `h − offset`) and the display formatter (`America/Chicago`, which honors DST) **agree** — a job window written as 08:00 local now encodes to the correct UTC instant and renders back as 08:00.

Caveat: like the original, this is a **fixed** offset, so it's only correct for summer (DST) dates. If you ever run it with a winter `--start-date`, the −5 constant would be off by an hour versus the `America/Chicago` display (which would show CST). For a June demo it's correct. If you want it bulletproof year-round I can compute the offset from the timezone per-date instead of using a constant — say the word.

The script still lives at `DHL_PL/scripts/generate-synthetic-data-wise.mjs` with its Coca-Cola/FEMSA cadence logic intact; only the locale (language + geography + timezone) changed.

Found the root cause. Class C's restriction string is:

```

It's an **`Allowed:`** list (the only 7 MSU equipment types that *can* do onsite shredding). But the parser (`parseDisallowedSet`, `build-rp-input.mjs:118`) treats **every** code it finds as *disallowed* — it ignores the `Allowed:`/`Disallowed:` prefix. So the logic inverts:

### CLAUDE (2026-07-01T12:11:27.562Z)

The complete diagnosis is now clear. The workbook uses **two** restriction formats, and the parser only handles one:

- **`Disallowed:` classes** (9, A, E, G, H, N, P, R, S, W, Y, Z) — listed codes are forbidden. Parser handles these correctly.
- **`Allowed:` classes** (C, T, U, V with codes; D, DEL, F empty) — listed codes are the *only* permitted ones. The parser treats them as *disallowed*, **inverting** the rule.

So **C (ONSITE), T (Data Tape Shred), U (Hard Drive Shred), and V (Pickup SITAD)** are all broken the same way — Class C is just the one the customer noticed. (D/DEL/F have empty lists → parse to empty → harmlessly "all allowed", which is why the bulk OFFSITE jobs still route fine.)

The fix belongs in `build-rp-input.mjs` (which builds `input_iron_mountain.json`; `json-to-csvs.mjs` just mirrors its `skills` into the CSVs). Let me read the exact parser + skill-assignment code.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-01T12:13:17.965Z)

The CSVs match the JSON: skill 3 is on **10/10 MSU vehicles and 0/40 non-MSU vehicles**.

## Summary

**Root cause** — a parser bug in `IRON_MOUNTAIN/scripts/build-rp-input.mjs`. The workbook's "Equipment Type Restrictions" come in two formats:
- `Disallowed: …` — listed equipment is forbidden
- `Allowed: …` — listed equipment is the *only* thing permitted

The old `parseDisallowedSet` ignored the keyword and treated **every** listed code as *disallowed*. For Class C (`Allowed: MSU-35, MSU, MSU-25, MDS3-*, MSU-EVHD`), this inverted the rule — the MSUs got excluded and every non-MSU truck qualified. That's exactly why Onsite Shredding jobs landed on box trucks, tippers, and vans.

**Fix** — made the parser keyword-aware (`parseRestriction` → `{mode, codes}`) and added `vehicleEligibleForClass`:
- `disallow` → eligible unless listed (unchanged)
- `allow` → eligible only if listed; an empty allow-list means "no restriction" (preserves the bulk D/DEL/F OFFSITE classes)

**Also fixed by the same change** (they had the identical inversion): **T** (Data Tape Shred SITAD), **U** (Hard Drive Shred SITAD), **V** (Pickup SITAD) — all `Allowed:` classes.

**Regenerated** `data/input_iron_mountain.json`, `data/jobs.csv`, `data/vehicles.csv`. Verified: all 22 Class C jobs require skill 3; skill 3 is now carried by exactly the 10 MSU/MDS3 units and no others.

**Not yet done:** re-running the optimization. The input is corrected, but the solution behind your comparison spreadsheet was produced from the *old* input. Want me to submit the regenerated `input_iron_mountain.json` to the Optimization v2 API and confirm Class C stops now fall only on MSU routes? (There's an `nb-optimization-submit` skill for exactly this.) I'll also flag one thing to check: only 10 MSU vehicles now serve all Class C + T/U/V shredding demand — if that capacity is tight, some of those jobs could come back unassigned, which we'd see in the new solution.

Added two CLI flags (defaulted to your values, so a bare re-run reproduces this):

## How these two interact (worth confirming this is the intent)
- `max_working_time: 34200` caps each route's active working time (travel + service + waiting) at 9.5h. The 18h `time_window` (04:00–22:00) still bounds the clock, but 9.5h is now the binding limit.
- `max_vehicle_overtime: 3600` lets the solver push a route up to **1 hour past** that cap (so effectively up to 10.5h) when needed to assign a job — typically at a penalty — rather than leaving it unassigned. So the effective hard ceiling per route becomes **10.5h**.

## Dependencies

`rolling_horizon.py` imports only one third-party package — **`numpy`**. Everything else (`argparse`, `datetime`, `json`, `math`, `os`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `collections`) ships with Python's standard library. I created `COCA_COLA-FEMSA/requirements.txt` pinning `numpy>=1.24`.

## Setup instructions

```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/COCA_COLA-FEMSA

# 1. Create the virtual environment
python3 -m venv .venv

# 2. Activate it (zsh/bash on macOS)
source .venv/bin/activate

# 3. Upgrade pip, then install dependencies
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

To confirm it worked:

```bash
python -c "import numpy; print('numpy', numpy.__version__)"
python data/rolling_horizon.py --help
```

When you're finished, `deactivate` returns to your normal shell.

1. **Not a Python dependency, but required at runtime:** the script shells out to a **Go** simulator (`go build -o <workdir>/simulator ./example/simulator`, invoked at `rolling_horizon.py:308-311`). The venv won't provide that — you'll need the Go toolchain installed and the `example/simulator` source available, or pass `--simulator <path>` to an existing binary. That path (`REPO_ROOT/example/simulator`) also suggests the script was written to run from a *different* repo root than this POC data folder, so double-check `--input`, `--dm`, and `--workdir` paths when you run it here.

2. **Python 3.14** is your default `python3`. numpy publishes wheels for it, so `pip install` should pull a prebuilt binary. If it ever tries to compile from source (no matching wheel), either let it build (needs a C compiler) or create the venv against an older interpreter, e.g. `python3.12 -m venv .venv`.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-08T12:51:40.125Z)

[tool: Bash — Apply all modifications to jim_original_input.json]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/COCA_COLA-FEMSA/data
cp jim_original_input.json jim_original_input.json.bak
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, datetime
TZ = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=-3))  # America/Sao_Paulo, no DST
MAX_WT = 26700

INCOMPAT = {
    'VEND. AUTOSSERVICO':    ['VEND. NOTURNO'],
    'VEND. OFF FRAGMENTADO': ['VEND. NOTURNO'],
    'VEND. NOTURNO':         ['VEND. AUTOSSERVICO', 'VEND. OFF FRAGMENTADO'],
}

def shift_window(tw):
    """Same calendar date (UTC-3), but 15:00-22:00 local."""
    day = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(tw[0], TZ).date()
    start = datetime.datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, 15, 0, tzinfo=TZ)
    end   = datetime.datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, 22, 0, tzinfo=TZ)
    return [int(start.timestamp()), int(end.timestamp())]

d = json.load(open('jim_original_input.json'))

# --- vehicles: drop time_window, add max_working_time ---
for v in d['vehicles']:
    v.pop('time_window', None)
    v['max_working_time'] = MAX_WT

# --- jobs ---
noturno_shifted = incompat_added = 0
for j in d['jobs']:
    load_type = j['description'].split('|')[-1]
    j['load_types'] = [load_type]
    inc = INCOMPAT.get(load_type)
    if inc:
        j['incompatible_load_types'] = list(inc)
        incompat_added += 1
    if 'NOTURNO' in j['description']:
        j['time_windows'] = [shift_window(tw) for tw in j['time_windows']]
        noturno_shifted += 1

with open('jim_original_input.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(', ', ': '))

print('vehicles updated (time_window removed, max_working_time added):', len(d['vehicles']))
print('jobs total                        :', len(d['jobs']))
print('NOTURNO jobs shifted to 15:00-22:00:', noturno_shifted)
print('jobs given incompatible_load_types :', incompat_added)
PY
```

import json, datetime, random
from collections import defaultdict
TZ=datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=-3))
random.seed(2024)   # reproducible

d=json.load(open('jim_original_input.json'))
V=d['vehicles']

# existing name pool (100 distinct surnames w/ initial)
name_pool=sorted({v['description'].rsplit('-',2)[0] for v in V})

# group existing vehicles by day, preserving insertion order of days
byday=defaultdict(list)
for v in V:
    byday[datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(v['time_window'][0],TZ).date()].append(v)

ADD_PER_DAY=50
next_id=max(v['id'] for v in V)+1
new_vehicles=[]
for day in sorted(byday):
    sample=byday[day][0]
    tw=sample['time_window']
    # week/dow tokens are identical across the day; take them from any member
    _, week, dow = sample['description'].rsplit('-',2)
    for _ in range(ADD_PER_DAY):
        name=random.choice(name_pool)
        new_vehicles.append({
            "id": next_id,
            "description": f"{name}-{week}-{dow}",
            "start_index": 0,
            "end_index": 0,
            "time_window": list(tw),
            "max_working_time": sample.get("max_working_time", 26700),
            "capacity": list(sample.get("capacity", [500])),
        })
        next_id+=1

d['vehicles']=V+new_vehicles
with open('jim_original_input.json','w') as f:
    json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(', ', ': '))

print('added vehicles      :', len(new_vehicles), f'({ADD_PER_DAY}/day x {len(byday)} days)')
print('total vehicles now  :', len(d['vehicles']))
print('new id range        :', new_vehicles[0]['id'], '..', new_vehicles[-1]['id'])
print('sample new vehicles :')
for v in new_vehicles[:4]: print('  ', json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False))
PY

Simulator writes [lng, lat]; femsa1 uses [lat, lng].\n    loc = step.get(\"location\")\n    if loc is not None:\n        out[\"location\"] = [loc[1], loc[0]]\n    out[\"location_index\"] = step.get(\"location_index\")\n    # Aggregate the shift's summary into the horizon summary.\n        ss = shift.get(\"summary\", {})\n        for k in SUMMARY_SUM_FIELDS:\n            summary[k] += ss.get(k, 0)\n\n    # Horizon-level unassigned = jobs never served by any shift.\n    unassigned = []\n    for jid, j in job_by_id.items():\n        if jid in served_ids:\n            continue\n        lat, lng = (float(x) for x in loc_strings[j[\"location_index\"]].split(\",\"))\n        unassigned.append({\n            \"id\": jid,\n            \"type\": \"job\",\n            \"location\": [lat, lng],\n            \"description\": j[\"description\"].split(\"|\")[0],  # Everything matches. Created **`merge_shifts_response.py`** and produced **`sim_runs/merged_response.json`**.

## What it does

Stitches the rolling-horizon per-shift results into a single NextBillion Optimization v2 response shaped exactly like `femsa1_response.json`:

- **Driver:** `combined_solution.json` supplies the day ordering and served/unassigned accounting; the rich route/step detail (steps, geometry, cost) is pulled from each matching `day_NN_output.json`. Zero-route days (weekends, no output file) contribute nothing.
- **Normalizes** each shift route/step to the femsa1 schema: step `location` emitted as `[lat, lng]` (simulator writes `[lng, lat]`), per-shift `location_index` preserved, `load` dropped, routes gain `profile` and drop `delivery`/`pickup`/`adopted_capacity`.
- **Aggregates** the horizon `summary` (sums cost/setup/service/duration/waiting_time/priority/distance; recomputes route & unassigned counts).
- **Unassigned** = jobs served by no shift, rendered `{id, type, location:[lat,lng], description(base id), reason}`.

## Validation (all pass)

- Top / result / summary / route / start-step / job-step / unassigned key sets **identical** to femsa1
- Coordinate order confirmed `[lat, lng]`
- **19,370 served + 4 unassigned = 19,374** total jobs — disjoint and complete
- Result: **20 shifts merged, 717 routes**, cost 10,726,468, distance 158,212,938 m

# → sim_runs/merged_response.json

### CLAUDE (2026-07-08T18:33:16.086Z)

The geometry support is complete and validated. Summary of what I added to `merge_shifts_response.py`:

## What's new

1. **Inline encoded-polyline codec** (`polyline_encode` / `polyline_decode`, precision-5) — verified against the canonical Google polyline example, exact round-trip. No external deps.

2. **Directions-API geometry generation** — for each merged route, takes its ordered step coordinates (`[lat, lng]`, depot → jobs → depot) and calls the NextBillion Directions API (`https://api.nextbillion.io/directions/json`) to get the road polyline, writing it to `route["geometry"]` to match femsa1's field.
   - **Chunking**: routes go up to 72 steps, so waypoints are split into overlapping chunks (≤48 intermediate each, default), decoded, joined on the shared boundary point, and re-encoded into one continuous polyline.
   - **Concurrency + retry**: `ThreadPoolExecutor` (default 8 parallel) with backoff retry on 429/5xx.
   - **Resilient**: a route that fails after retries keeps empty geometry + a `_geom_error` note; the run still completes and reports `ok/failed/skipped` counts.

3. **CLI flags**: `--geometry/--no-geometry` (default on), `--key` (defaults to `$NB_API_KEY`), `--mode`, `--max-waypoints`, `--concurrency`, `--geom-timeout`.

## To actually generate geometry

It needs a live key (I don't have one in this environment — with no key it warns and leaves geometry empty, as shown):

```bash
cd COCA_COLA-FEMSA/data
NB_API_KEY=your_key python3 merge_shifts_response.py
# → sim_runs/merged_response.json with route["geometry"] populated
```

Two notes worth flagging:
- **Cost**: 700 routes × ~1–2 Directions calls each ≈ 700–900 API requests per run. If you want to trial it first, add a quick `--max-waypoints`-style limiter or run against a copied subset; say the word and I'll add a `--limit-routes N` flag for a cheap smoke test.
- The current `sim_runs/` day outputs are the **re-solved** ones (700 routes now, vs 717 before) — so this reflects your latest constraints. If you re-run `rolling_horizon.py` again, re-run the merge afterward.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T12:48:57.010Z)

The live Clustering API call works end-to-end — 40 real jobs submitted, clustered, and zoned successfully. Implementation complete.

## What I added to `rolling_horizon.py`

**A per-shift clustering step** that runs *before* each `day_{xx}_input.json` is written:

1. **`cluster_pool_zones()`** — submits the shift's pool jobs to the NB Clustering API (`POST /clustering`), polls `/clustering/result`, and returns `{job_id: zone}`. The request matches your spec:
   ```json
   {
     "options": {"routing": {"mode": "car"}, "objective": {"travel_cost": "air_distance"}},
     "clusters": [{"id": 1, "max_quantity": 500}, ... {"id": 10, "max_quantity": 500}],
     "jobs": [{"id": ..., "location_index": ..., "quantity": 1}],
     "locations": ["lat,lng", ...]
   }
   ```
   10 clusters (ids 1–10, `max_quantity: 500`); cluster `id` → **zone `id-1`** so zones are 0-indexed.

2. **In `build_shift_input`**:
   - Each job gets `zones: [zone]` (0–9) from the clustering result. Clustering leaves a job unassigned → defaults to zone 0 (with a logged count).
   - Each vehicle gets `allowed_zones: [i % 10]`, cycling **0,1,…,9,0,1,…** across the day's fleet.

3. **CLI flags**: `--zones/--no-zones` (default on), `--nb-key` (defaults to `$NB_API_KEY`), `--num-zones 10`, `--zone-max-qty 500`, `--zone-mode car`, `--zone-travel-cost air_distance`.

## Verified

- Job zones set correctly, `allowed_zones` rotate `[0,1,…,9,0,1]` ✓
- Clusters payload = 10 × `max_quantity 500` ✓
- `--no-zones` path adds neither field ✓
- **Live API** call succeeded: 40 jobs → zoned across the clusters ✓

## Run it

NB_API_KEY=opensesame .venv/bin/python3 rolling_horizon.py

- **options**: taken from the first shift

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T13:19:41.570Z)

Now I can answer definitively.

## No — we're not including top-level zone definitions, and for our approach we don't need to.

**What's in the files:** The day inputs (and the combined `input.json`) carry only the **ID-based** zone assignment:
- `job.zones = [id]` (integer zone IDs, 0–9)
- `vehicle.allowed_zones = [id]`

There is **no top-level `zones` array** — never was, in the individual files or the combined one. The combine script carried through everything that existed; there was simply nothing to carry.

**Why that's valid.** NextBillion supports two independent ways to zone:

| Approach | What you provide | Purpose |
|----------|-----------------|---------|
| **ID-based** (what we use) | `job.zones` IDs + `vehicle.allowed_zones` IDs | Optimizer matches vehicle↔job **directly by integer ID** |
| **Geometry-based** | top-level `zones: [{id, geometry\|geofence_id}]` | Optimizer **auto-allocates** jobs to zones by their location |

The spec is explicit that these are alternatives — from the `job.zones` description:

> *"Zone IDs provided here will **override any zone geometries** provided in the `zones` attribute and these IDs will be used for allocating appropriate vehicles."*

So because every job has an explicit `zones` ID and every vehicle an `allowed_zones` ID, the optimizer never needs the geometry. A top-level `zones` definition is **only** required if you drop the per-job IDs and want jobs auto-assigned by falling inside polygon/geofence boundaries.

## So the combined input is complete as-is.

If you *did* want to add the top-level definitions anyway (e.g., for documentation, or to switch to geometry-based assignment), each zone object looks like:

```json
"zones": [
  { "id": 0, "geometry": { "type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[lng,lat], ...]] } },
  ...
]
```

with `geometry` (a Polygon/MultiPolygon) or a `geofence_id` from the Geofence API. Note the clustering results already contain a convex-hull polyline per cluster (`cluster.geometry`) — I could decode those into 10 zone polygons and emit a top-level `zones` array to accompany the IDs. Want me to add that (either to the rolling-horizon step or as an option on the combine script)?

 "new_string": "import argparse\nimport glob\nimport json\nimport os\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\nBASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n\n\ndef convex_hull(points):\n    \"\"\"Andrew's monotone chain. points: iterable of (x, y). Returns the hull\n    vertices in counter-clockwise order (not closed). <3 unique points -> [] .\"\"\"\n    pts = sorted(set(points))\n    if len(pts) < 3:\n        return []\n\n    def cross(o, a, b):\n        return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])\n\n    lower = []\n    for p in pts:\n        while len(lower) >= 2 and cross(lower[-2], lower[-1], p) <= 0:\n            lower.pop()\n        lower.append(p)\n    upper = []\n    for p in reversed(pts):\n        while len(upper) >= 2 and cross(upper[-2], upper[-1], p) <= 0:\n            upper.pop()\n        upper.append(p)\n    return lower[:-1] + upper[:-1]\n\n\ndef build_zone_polygons(jobs):\n    \"\"\"Top-level `zones` array: one Polygon per zone id, the convex hull of the\n    [lng,lat] coordinates of the jobs carrying that zone id. Zones with fewer\n    than 3 distinct points are skipped (no valid polygon).\"\"\"\n    by_zone = defaultdict(list)\n    for j in jobs:\n        z = j.get(\"zones\")\n        loc = j.get(\"location\")  # [lng, lat]\n        if z and loc is not None:\n            by_zone[z[0]].append((loc[0], loc[1]))\n    zones, skipped = [], []\n    for zid in sorted(by_zone):\n        hull = convex_hull(by_zone[zid])\n        if len(hull) < 3:\n            skipped.append(zid)\n            continue\n        ring = [[x, y] for (x, y) in hull]\n        ring.append(ring[0])  # geoJSON rings must be closed\n        zones.append({\"id\": zid, \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Polygon\", \"coordinates\": [ring]}})\n    return zones, skipped"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T13:59:49.689Z)

Root cause found. Your direct image redeploy wiped the entire Terraform-managed runtime config. Two things changed on the live revision:

1. **No `env` block at all** — the `NB_API_KEY` secret binding (plus `DD_DATA_FILE`/`DD_GEOCODE_CACHE`) is gone. That's why the app hits `process.env.NB_API_KEY` → undefined → *"NB_API_KEY not configured"*.
2. **Wrong service account** — the revision runs as the default compute SA (`[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER]-compute@…`), but `secretAccessor` on the secret is granted only to `dd-demo-sa@…`. So even adding the binding back requires fixing the SA too.

The good news: the secret `dd-demo-nb-api-key` exists (version 1, enabled) and `dd-demo-sa` already has access — nothing to recreate.

This happens because `gcloud run deploy --image …` builds a revision from the image alone; it doesn't know about Terraform's env/SA settings.

## Fix — two options

**A. Durable (recommended): re-apply Terraform with the image pinned.** Restores env, SA, timeouts, and reconciles the drift:
```bash
cd DIESEL_DIRECT/terraform
terraform apply -var image=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[GCP_PROJECT]/dieseldirect/dd-demo:latest
```
⚠️ Don't run a bare `terraform apply` — `image` is commented out in `terraform.tfvars`, so it would revert you to GCP's hello-world sample (the same trap as GLWAS). Pin `image` on the CLI, or set it in `terraform.tfvars`.

**B. Immediate one-liner (no Terraform): patch the live service.** Sets the correct SA, binds the secret, and restores the other env vars on the current image:
```bash
gcloud run services update dd-demo --region us-central1 --project [GCP_PROJECT] \
  --service-account [EMAIL] \
  --update-secrets NB_API_KEY=dd-demo-nb-api-key:latest \
  --update-env-vars DD_DATA_FILE=/data/routes.xlsx,DD_GEOCODE_CACHE=/data/geocode_cache.json
```

Option B fixes it fastest but leaves Terraform state out of sync (a later `terraform apply` would still need the pinned image). Option A is the clean path.

Returns hull\n    vertices counter-clockwise (not closed); <3 unique points -> [].\"\"\"\n    pts = sorted(set(points))\n    if len(pts) < 3:\n        return []\n\n    def cross(o, a, b):\n        return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])\n\n    lower = []\n    for p in pts:\n        while len(lower) >= 2 and cross(lower[-2], lower[-1], p) <= 0:\n            lower.pop()\n        lower.append(p)\n    upper = []\n    for p in reversed(pts):\n        while len(upper) >= 2 and cross(upper[-2], upper[-1], p) <= 0:\n            upper.pop()\n        upper.append(p)\n    return lower[:-1] + upper[:-1]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Per-shift MVRO input\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef build_shift_input(pool, vehicles, data, durations, distances, zone_cfg=None, day_index=0):"

1. **The local solver doesn't implement `max_working_time`.** It's simply not a field it knows, so it's dropped on parse. (The real NB Optimization v2 API *does* enforce it — our input is correct and would be honored there.)
2. With nothing capping working time, the solver fills each route up to the only time bound it *does* honor — the vehicle `time_window`, which we widened to **07:00–22:30 (15.5 h)**.
3. The overflow is **service time**, not driving: 76% of routes exceed 26,700 s on working time, but only **1%** exceed it on driving time. Routes carry 13–17 jobs whose service alone (24,000–31,200 s) already blows past the 7.42 h cap.

So it's a **simulator limitation**, not a bug in the input generation or the carry-through.

```bash
cd COCA_COLA-FEMSA/data
.venv/bin/python3 combine_day_inputs.py \
  --description "FEMSA combined 4-week single-shot input (from rolling-horizon day shifts)"
```

It stitches the `sim_runs/day_*_input.json` shift files into one `sim_runs/input.json` — merging locations (deduped), jobs (deduped by id), vehicles, `options`, and the top-level `zones` array (concatenated from each shift's unique-id zones).

Flags (all optional, sensible defaults):
- `--workdir sim_runs` — where the day files live
- `--glob 'day_*_input.json'` — which files to combine
- `--output sim_runs/input.json` — destination
- `--description '...'` — top-level description
- `--zones / --no-zones` — emit the top-level zones array (default on)

Note the IDE has `data/input.json` open — that's a *different* file (the one with the original vehicle time windows). The combine script writes to `sim_runs/input.json` by default to avoid clobbering it; pass `--output` if you want it elsewhere.

    vs=d.get(vehkey) or d.get('vehicles') or []
    c=Counter()

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T17:13:33.994Z)

[tool: Bash — Insert break into each vehicle]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/IRON_MOUNTAIN/data
cp input_iron_mountain.json input_iron_mountain.json.bak
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");
const OFFSET=-6; // MDT
const path="input_iron_mountain.json";
const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path,"utf8"));

function breakWindow(startUnix){
  // local (MDT) calendar date of the vehicle shift start
  const local=new Date((startUnix + OFFSET*3600)*1000);
  const y=local.getUTCFullYear(), mo=local.getUTCMonth(), day=local.getUTCDate();
  const s=Math.floor(Date.UTC(y,mo,day,11 - OFFSET,0,0)/1000); // 11:00 MDT
  const e=Math.floor(Date.UTC(y,mo,day,13 - OFFSET,0,0)/1000); // 13:00 MDT
  return [s,e];
}

let n=0;
for(const v of d.vehicles){
  const [s,e]=breakWindow(v.time_window[0]);
  v.breaks=[{ id:1, description:"break", time_windows:[[s,e]], service:1800 }];
  n++;
}
fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(d,null,2)+"\n");
console.log("vehicles updated with break:", n);
// verify one
const b=d.vehicles[0].breaks[0];
const fmt=t=>new Date((t + OFFSET*3600)*1000).toISOString().replace(".000Z"," MDT").slice(11);
console.log("break:", JSON.stringify(b));
console.log("window local MDT:", fmt(b.time_windows[0][0]), "->", fmt(b.time_windows[0][1]), "| duration(s):", b.service);
'
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T17:21:22.438Z)

Happy path still works — 40 jobs zoned cleanly. Fix is complete and verified.

## What was wrong

`rolling_horizon.py`'s clustering step polled the NB Clustering API only **120× at 3 s = 6 minutes**, then raised `clustering timed out`. A large daily pool (up to 3,000–4,000 jobs) can take longer than that to cluster, and a single slow/transient response aborted the entire multi-hour run.

## What I changed (`cluster_pool_zones`)

1. **Longer timeout**: default poll budget raised from 6 min → **~20 min** (400 polls × 3 s).
2. **Configurable**: new flags `--cluster-poll-max` and `--cluster-poll-interval` (threaded through `zone_cfg`).
3. **Transient-error resilience**: a network blip on a single poll no longer crashes the run — it retries up to 5 consecutive failures before giving up.
4. **Better diagnostics**: on timeout the error now reports the **last status** and **task id**, so you can tell "still processing" (bump the timeout) from "stuck/errored."

## To re-run

```bash
cd COCA_COLA-FEMSA/data
NB_API_KEY=... .venv/bin/python3 rolling_horizon.py
# if a huge shift still times out, raise the budget:
#   --cluster-poll-max 800     (≈40 min)
# or lighten each clustering call:
#   --max-pool 1500
```

Two things worth flagging about the design: clustering runs **once per non-empty shift** synchronously (~20 calls), so the whole run is inherently long and any one timeout is costly — a smaller `--max-pool` makes each clustering call faster and the run more robust. And if the new error message shows `last status='pending'` even after 20 min, that's the API genuinely taking longer, not a bug — just raise `--cluster-poll-max`.

Want me to commit this fix (rolling_horizon.py) and the IRON_MOUNTAIN break change together?

node -e '
const XLSX=require("../node_modules/xlsx");
const fs=require("fs");
const wb=XLSX.readFile("data/IM Sample Data for Demo_030626.xlsx");
const rows=n=>XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[n]);

// --- replicate build-rp-input.mjs skill logic ---
function parseRestriction(text){
  const codes=new Set();
  if(!text) return {mode:"disallow",codes};
  const s=String(text);
  const mode=/^\s*allowed/i.test(s)?"allow":"disallow";
  const i=s.indexOf(":"); const body=i>=0?s.slice(i+1):s;
  for(const m of body.matchAll(/([A-Z0-9-]+)\s*-\s*[^,]+/g)) codes.add(m[1]);
  return {mode,codes};
}
function eligible(typeCode,r){
  if(r.mode==="allow") return r.codes.size===0||r.codes.has(typeCode);
  return !r.codes.has(typeCode);
}
const oc=rows("Order Classes");
const orderClassById=new Map(oc.map(r=>[String(r.ID),r]));
const orderClassIds=Array.from(orderClassById.keys()).sort();
const skillOf=new Map(); orderClassIds.forEach((id,i)=>skillOf.set(id,i+1));
const restr=new Map();
for(const id of orderClassIds) restr.set(id, parseRestriction(orderClassById.get(id)["Equipment Type Restrictions"]));
const FORCE_ALLOWED={V:["RM20"]};
for(const [ocId,types] of Object.entries(FORCE_ALLOWED)){
  const r=restr.get(ocId); if(!r) continue;
  for(const t of types){ if(r.mode==="allow") r.codes.add(t); else r.codes.delete(t); }
}
const typeCode="SHRED24";
const skills=[];
for(const ocId of orderClassIds) if(eligible(typeCode,restr.get(ocId))) skills.push(skillOf.get(ocId));

// cube capacity for SHRED24
const et=rows("Equipment Types").find(r=>String(r.ID)==="SHRED24");
const cube=Number(et.Cube)||0;

// --- pull CD-S2 depot index + shift window + break from an existing CD-S2 vehicle ---
const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("data/input_iron_mountain.json","utf8"));
const ref=d.vehicles.find(v=>v.metadata && v.metadata.depot==="CD-S2") || d.vehicles[0];
console.log("reference CD-S2 vehicle:", ref.id, "start_index:", ref.start_index, "tw:", JSON.stringify(ref.time_window), "mwt:", ref.max_working_time);
console.log("SHRED24 cube:", cube, "| skills:", JSON.stringify(skills), "| n skills:", skills.length);

const veh={
  id:"14784",
  description:`SHRED24 - Shred 24\x27|CD-S2`,
  start_index:ref.start_index,
  end_index:ref.end_index,
  capacity:[cube],
  time_window:[...ref.time_window],
  max_working_time:ref.max_working_time,
  skills,
  metadata:{ depot:"CD-S2", equipment_type:"SHRED24", regions:"CD-SS - Denver" },
  breaks:[{ id:1, description:"break", time_windows:[[...ref.breaks[0].time_windows[0]]], service:1800 }]
};
d.vehicles.push(veh);
fs.writeFileSync("data/input_iron_mountain.json", JSON.stringify(d,null,2)+"\n");
console.log("\nadded vehicle:", JSON.stringify(veh,null,1));
console.log("total vehicles now:", d.vehicles.length);
'

## One thing to flag — it can't do shredding jobs

Despite being a "Shred 24'" truck, per the source `Order Classes` restrictions SHRED24 is **excluded** from the four SITAD/shred classes:

- **C** (Onsite Shredding) — allowed only to MSU units
- **T** (Data Tape Shred), **U** (Hard Drive Shred) — allowed only to MSU/MDS3 hard-drive shredders
- **V** (Pickup SITAD) — allowed only to ALM/RM20 equipment

So it covers 15 of 19 order classes (all the general document/box work) but **not** the specialized shred classes, because those require specific MSU/MDS3/ALM equipment and SHRED24 isn't on their `Allowed:` lists. If you expected this truck to serve onsite-shredding (Class C) jobs, that's a source-data restriction — let me know and I can add the relevant skill(s) manually.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T20:50:04.531Z)

[tool: Bash — Add vehicle 12532 and confirm JSON matches image]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/IRON_MOUNTAIN
cp data/input_iron_mountain.json data/input_iron_mountain.json.bak
node -e '
const XLSX=require("../node_modules/xlsx");
const fs=require("fs");
const wb=XLSX.readFile("data/IM Sample Data for Demo_030626.xlsx");
const rows=n=>XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[n]);
function parseRestriction(text){const codes=new Set();if(!text)return{mode:"disallow",codes};const s=String(text);const mode=/^\s*allowed/i.test(s)?"allow":"disallow";const i=s.indexOf(":");const body=i>=0?s.slice(i+1):s;for(const m of body.matchAll(/([A-Z0-9-]+)\s*-\s*[^,]+/g))codes.add(m[1]);return{mode,codes};}
function eligible(tc,r){if(r.mode==="allow")return r.codes.size===0||r.codes.has(tc);return !r.codes.has(tc);}

// source row for 12532
const src=rows("Equipment").find(r=>String(r.ID)==="12532");
const typeCode=String(src["Equipment Type"]).match(/^([A-Z0-9-]+)/)[1];
const et=rows("Equipment Types").find(r=>String(r.ID)===typeCode);
const cube=Number(et.Cube)||0;

// skills (build-rp-input logic)
const oc=rows("Order Classes");
const byId=new Map(oc.map(r=>[String(r.ID),r]));
const ids=Array.from(byId.keys()).sort();
const skillOf=new Map(); ids.forEach((id,i)=>skillOf.set(id,i+1));
const restr=new Map(); for(const id of ids) restr.set(id,parseRestriction(byId.get(id)["Equipment Type Restrictions"]));
const FA={V:["RM20"]};
for(const [ocId,types] of Object.entries(FA)){const r=restr.get(ocId);if(!r)continue;for(const t of types){if(r.mode==="allow")r.codes.add(t);else r.codes.delete(t);}}
const skills=[]; for(const ocId of ids) if(eligible(typeCode,restr.get(ocId))) skills.push(skillOf.get(ocId));

const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("data/input_iron_mountain.json","utf8"));
if(d.vehicles.some(v=>String(v.id)==="12532")){console.log("already present");process.exit(1);}
const ref=d.vehicles.find(v=>v.metadata&&v.metadata.depot==="CD-S2");
const veh={
  id:"12532",
  description:`${src.Description}|CD-S2`,
  start_index:ref.start_index, end_index:ref.end_index,
  capacity:[cube],
  time_window:[...ref.time_window],
  max_working_time:ref.max_working_time,
  skills,
  metadata:{depot:"CD-S2",equipment_type:typeCode,regions:"CD-SS - Denver"},
  breaks:[{id:1,description:"break",time_windows:[[...ref.breaks[0].time_windows[0]]],service:1800}]
};
d.vehicles.push(veh);
fs.writeFileSync("data/input_iron_mountain.json", JSON.stringify(d,null,2)+"\n");
console.log("added 12532:",typeCode,"cube",cube,"| skills("+skills.length+"):",JSON.stringify(skills));
console.log("total vehicles now:", d.vehicles.length);
'
echo
node -e '
const d=require("./data/input_iron_mountain.json");
const inJson=new Set(d.vehicles.map(v=>String(v.id)));
const image=[...new Set("12851,12408,DFLT,15071,12418,14162,12853,11779,12155,11582,12584,15195,12303,12339,14784,12303,15191,13476,12945,12008,15192,14707,12341,12329,12532".split(","))];
const ids=d.vehicles.map(v=>String(v.id));
console.log("JSON valid | vehicles:",d.vehicles.length,"| dup ids?",ids.length!==new Set(ids).size);
console.log("image IDs missing from JSON:", image.filter(id=>!inJson.has(id)).join(", ")||"none — JSON now matches the image");
'
rm -f data/input_iron_mountain.json.bak && echo "backup removed"
